name: retry_with_escalation
one_line: Retry plainly first; when that stops helping, change the request.
how_it_works: Spend a plain retry budget first, because most failures clear on their own and escalation costs more.
When it runs out, mark the request escalated and try again.
Exhausting the ladder stops the run.
pros: The only policy here that recovers a failure caused by the request itself, which no amount of retrying can fix.
Escalates only after plain retries fail, so a transient failure costs zero escalations.
The ladder is a field, not a subclass, which is the same shape as this runtime's own escalation ladder.
cons: More expensive than plain retry on every failure it does not fix, because it pays the plain budget and then the escalated one.
Escalating changes the request, so the successful attempt is not the attempt that was specified. That has to be recorded or the run is not reproducible.
Two budgets to set instead of one.
pick_this_when: Failures have more than one cause and some are request-shaped.
You can express a stronger version of the same request.
avoid_when: Every failure is transient. The ladder is then pure overhead.

evidence.note: the only arm that recovered every recoverable shape, and it spent zero escalations on the shapes a plain retry already fixed
